outcome: adherence to intermittent pneumatic compression devices (IPCD)
cohort: Sixty-seven women requiring postnatal thromboprophylaxis completed questionnaires and diaries.
finding: Adherence to enoxaparin therapy was relatively high (82.4%), but self-reported adherence to anti-embolic stockings (AES) was sub-optimal (24% never wore them once home) due to reasons such as mobility, feeling hot, and feeling like circulation was cut off.
mod_finding: Women reported high acceptance of IPCD post-caesarean section and would be happy for them to be applied again in future deliveries.
cross-section timing: Postnatal period during which thromboprophylaxis was required and administered.
